prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the subjects corresponding to the BASIC TRAINING modules and those of the second year of the INDUSTRIAL BRANCH COMMON module.
Solid knowledge of Electrical Technology, Electronic Technology, and Automation and Control is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Interpret and modify control and power diagrams of electrical and pneumatic automation systems.
Analyze, design, and implement industrial automated systems using Programmable Logic Controllers.
Apply different types of sensors and actuators in process automation.
Know and integrate exploitation and supervision devices and technologies for automated systems.
Know and understand the basic operation of robotic systems.
Identify the objectives and limitations, application technologies, components, and their relationship in automated systems.
Apply elements of technologies based on wired logic (electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic) and programmed logic for the implementation of industrial automation systems.
Analyze and design automation systems with standard methodologies such as GRAFCET, Petri Nets, or GEMMA.
Develop process control applications based on programmable logic controllers.
Apply basic tools for the exploitation and supervision of automated systems.

syllabus_topics: Automated systems.
Wired logic-based automation: electrical, pneumatic, and hydraulic systems.
Fundamentals and application of robotic systems.
Programmable Logic Controllers.
Methodologies for analysis and design of automated systems.
Standard programming of programmable logic controllers.
Exploitation and supervision of automated systems.
Topic 1. Fundamental components of an automated system.
Topic 2. Low voltage switchgear.
Topic 3. Electronic starters and variable speed drives.
Topic 4. Standardization of diagrams and normalization. Basic diagrams.
Topic 5. Data acquisition.
Topic 6. Electromagnetic compatibility (EMC).
Topic 7. Introduction to Industrial Pneumatics. Compressed air theory.
Topic 8. Air compression, distribution, and treatment.
Topic 9. Actuators. Special, rotary, and gripper actuators.
Topic 10. Valves.
Topic 11. Vacuum. Pneumatic symbology.
Topic 12. The Programmable Logic Controller.
Topic 13. PLC Architecture.
Topic 14. Basic programming concepts. Tasks and POUs.
Topic 15. Programming languages and instructions (IEC 61131-3).
Topic 16. SFC - GRAFCET language.
Topic 17. Introduction to Industrial Robotics.

assessment_methods.method: Final Exam Automation with Programmed Logic and Industrial Robotics (P3)
Practical Work Automation of industrial process (T1)

assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary call, it is mandatory to obtain a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 in the final exam (P3) and a minimum of 4 out of 10 in the practical work (T1). If these minimums are met, the final grade (N) is calculated as: N = 0.15*P1 + 0.05*PR1 + 0.15*P2 + 0.05*PR2 + 0.35*P3 + 0.25*T1. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, the theoretical part is evaluated by a single exam (PEX) and the practical part by the submission and defense of the Practical Work (TEX). It is mandatory to obtain at least 5 points out of 10 in the theoretical part and 4 points out of 10 in the practical work (TEX) to pass. If these minimums are reached, the final grade (N) is calculated as: N = 0.2*P1 + 0.2*P2 + 0.35*PEX + 0.25*TEX; otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. Practical exams require attendance at practice sessions to be taken. Partial exam grades (P1/P2) and laboratory practical exams are valid for the current academic year if a minimum of 5 is obtained, otherwise, they are re-evaluated in the final or extraordinary exam.
